text.p: Indonesian brokerage firm PT ING Baring Securities on Monday maintained its "buy" recommendation for PT Indonesian Satellite Corporation (Indosat) following a 3.6-percent increase of its collection rate from its five-top destinations.
ING Baring said in its latest research report the new international telephone collection rates, implemented by the government on January 1, were positive for the company.
"We believe this is positive for the company and maintain our 'buy' recommendation with a six-month price target of 7,500 rupiah," it said.
Indosat fell 50 rupiah to close at 6,975 rupiah on a turnover of 553,500 shares on Monday.
The report said the new rates for the major destinations were, however, still lower than reciprocal tariffs.
Indosat's tariffs on its major routes are formulated such that the outgoing tariff from Indonesia to a correspondent country was lower than the other way round, it said.
"Furthermore, we can safely assume that traffic in the top five destinations was being generated by business users who are less price sensitive than private or household users," it said.
"Hence, we do not expect a negative impact on Indosat's call volume on these routes," the report said.
ING Baring said Indosat's top five destinations were Singapore, the United States, Japan, Australia and Hong Kong -- which account for some 60 percent of its total traffic volume.
